\chapter{The correspondence with the C code}\label{chap:correspondence}

The model is checked against ratpoints v3.1.1 (commit \texttt{1a998538dfa8}). The C files below are those of the library and \texttt{main.c}, whose parts that the command-line program does not mirror are to be excluded. Every line of code of them lies in at most one recorded range: a range is either modelled by the Lean declarations named, or excluded from the model with a reason. Each recorded range is checked against the text it had when it was reviewed.

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.hornerSteps}: computed from \texttt{Ratpoints.maxBitsInPrime} as the macro computes it from \texttt{RATPOINTS\_MAX\_BITS\_IN\_PRIME}, with \texttt{64} for \texttt{LONG\_LENGTH}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{1683}{1697}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrime?}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrime?}: the prime \texttt{p} itself, for its index \texttt{pn} in the table \texttt{prime}; the table a fresh array of \texttt{p + 1} entries, for the integers that \texttt{examine\_prime} takes from the buffer \texttt{int\_next} and hands back through \texttt{is\_f\_square\_p}, and the coefficients a fresh array returned with the entry, for the array \texttt{coeffs\_mod\_p} of its caller, which it fills; one loop over the residues, for the two loops of the two branches of the schedule of Horner's rule, between which \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.hornerBarrett} chooses for each residue; the exit \texttt{-{}1} as \texttt{none}, and the codes \texttt{0}, \texttt{1} and \texttt{2} returned with the entry, the coefficients and the density, as natural numbers, the entry made and returned for the code \texttt{0} too, where \texttt{examine\_prime} makes none, and the density \texttt{0.0} for that code, which \texttt{examine\_prime} does not compute; the fields \texttt{p}, \texttt{mask} and \texttt{nf} of the record \texttt{prec\_entry} of the ranking, which \texttt{examine\_prime} sets with the density (lines 1782-1785), made by the caller from the table, the position of the prime and the code (\texttt{Ratpoints.ModulusCandidate.ofPrime}); the entry is a fresh value, for the space that \texttt{examine\_prime} takes from the buffer of the sieve entries (\texttt{se\_next}), and returned, where \texttt{examine\_prime} stores it in the field \texttt{ssp} of \texttt{prec\_entry}; it keeps only \texttt{p}, the table and the inverses (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry}), and no rows: the table of rows of the prime, with the row of \texttt{0} from the build and the others absent (lines 1820-1821, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.primeRows}), is made in the store of the run by the loop of the tables when the prime says something (\texttt{Ratpoints.examineInLoop}), and for a prime that the third stage takes into the pool by the end of the choice (\texttt{Ratpoints.choiceEnd}, with \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.addTables}); the fields \texttt{init}, \texttt{nf} and \texttt{pw} that \texttt{examine\_prime} sets (lines 1800 and 1817) and its reciprocal \texttt{magic} (line 1808) are those of the sieve entry of the prime (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry}), of which the prime is the single factor, made by the entries that the choice of the moduli makes (\texttt{Ratpoints.primeEntry}), which set the reciprocal there, and so are the bias \texttt{bias}, the inverse \texttt{rbainv} of \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaLength}, the density and the count of factors (lines 1811 and 1815-1817), which they set there with the formulas of these lines.)

it keeps only \texttt{p}, the table and the inverses (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry}), and no rows: the table of rows of the prime, with the row of \texttt{0} from the build and the others absent (lines 1820-1821, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.primeRows}), is made in the store of the run by the loop of the tables when the prime says something (\texttt{Ratpoints.examineInLoop}), and for a prime that the third stage takes into the pool by the end of the choice (\texttt{Ratpoints.choiceEnd}, with \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.addTables}); the fields \texttt{init}, \texttt{nf} and \texttt{pw} that \texttt{examine\_prime} sets (lines 1800 and 1817) and its reciprocal \texttt{magic} (line 1808) are those of the sieve entry of the prime (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry}), of which the prime is the single factor, made by the entries that the choice of the moduli makes (\texttt{Ratpoints.primeEntry}), which set the reciprocal there, and so are the bias \texttt{bias}, the inverse \texttt{rbainv} of \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaLength}, the density and the count of factors (lines 1811 and 1815-1817), which they set there with the formulas of these lines.)

the bounds of the search intervals an array, for the struct \texttt{rp\_intervals} with its pointers \texttt{bd} and \texttt{end}, which \texttt{sift} reaches through the field \texttt{iv} of the sieving thread, which \texttt{worker\_init} clears (line 3130) and \texttt{run\_block} sets for each block (line 3913; here \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.runBlock}, which passes the array of the run on); one call of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.setRows}, for the two calls with the flag \texttt{shared} a constant, between which the pool of threads chooses, which the model does not have; the store of the tables of rows passed and returned, for the arrays \texttt{sieve} of the entries of the arguments, which \texttt{sift} reaches through \texttt{sieve\_list} and which keep the rows built for the rest of the run; the end \texttt{sp1} of the first stage, the entries \texttt{es} and the reciprocals \texttt{mgs} of the first two stages, the entries \texttt{es3} of the third stage and their reciprocals \texttt{mgs3} as arguments, for the numbers \texttt{sp1}, \texttt{sp2} and \texttt{sp3} that the sieving thread keeps (\texttt{worker\_init}), the entries \texttt{sieve\_list[0], …, sieve\_list[sp2 -{} 1]}, the array \texttt{magics} of the arguments, which \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} reads, and the entries \texttt{sieve\_list[sp2], …, sieve\_list[sp3 -{} 1]} and the reciprocals \texttt{magics[sp2], …, magics[sp3 -{} 1]}, which \texttt{fill\_checks} reads, the cut points of the decision of the block (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.runBlock}); the residues \texttt{bp} and the class \texttt{cl} as values, for the pointers \texttt{bp\_list} and \texttt{cls}, and the array \texttt{offsets} of the row offsets of the run as an argument, which the C code reaches through the pointer \texttt{offset} of the class; the thunk of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.fillChecks}, for the table \texttt{checks} of the sieving thread, which \texttt{fill\_checks} fills, and its flag \texttt{stage3\_filled}, which \texttt{sift} clears; the thunk of the products \texttt{w}, for the flag \texttt{compute\_bc}, which \texttt{sift} sets and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} clears when it computes the products; the counters \texttt{cnt} passed and returned, for those of the sieving thread, the count \texttt{sifts} one up at the start (line 3461); the delivery \texttt{r} passed and returned, for the pointers \texttt{info} and \texttt{wk-{}>quit}, which \texttt{worker\_init} clears, and the count \texttt{total} that \texttt{sift} keeps from zero and returns; the arguments of the run passed explicitly, for the pointer \texttt{args} of the sieving thread (\texttt{rp-{}private.h:574}), which \texttt{worker\_init} sets and through which \texttt{sift} reads them; no pool, slot and stop flag of a thread of the pool, the flag by which the pool of threads tells it to abandon its block (\texttt{pool}, \texttt{slot}, \texttt{stop}, \texttt{rp-{}private.h:584}, excluded with the threads); natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; no measurements of the phases (\texttt{RP\_SIFT\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_SETUP\_TIC} and their \texttt{TOC}) and no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{3149}{3170}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.setRows}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.setRows}: a list of the moduli with their rows and offsets, for the array of sieve specs \texttt{ssp} that \texttt{set\_rows} fills; the empty array for the null pointer of a row not built yet; the start set to \texttt{0}, where the C code leaves the field as it is until the first stage sets it; the end \texttt{p} also for a row not built yet, where the C code adds \texttt{p} to the null pointer; the row read plainly, for the acquire load that the flag \texttt{shared} chooses when threads share the tables of rows; the store of the tables of rows of the run as an argument, for the arrays \texttt{sieve} of the entries that the pointers in \texttt{sieve\_list} reach; the array of the row offsets of the run as an argument, which the C code reaches through the pointer \texttt{offset} of the class, and a class without a row of offsets (none, for \texttt{NULL}), which the run never sifts, reads the offsets from position \texttt{0}; natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{3219}{3221}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.IntervalBounds}

\item \csource{find_points.c}{3231}{3238}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.exactScale}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.exactScale}: the 128-bit product, sum and shift on two 64-bit halves, the high half of the product by \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.mulHi}, for the \texttt{unsigned \_\_int128} of the arm that the builds of the model compile (the compiler defines \texttt{\_\_SIZEOF\_INT128\_\_}, and \texttt{RP\_NO\_INT128} is not set), which Lean core does not have; the other arm (lines 3239-3256), for a build without a 128-bit type, is excluded; the \texttt{long} \texttt{b} converted to a 64-bit word, as the C code converts it to an \texttt{unsigned long}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{3239}{3256}: excluded (other): the arm of exact\_scale for a build without a 128-bit type or with RP\_NO\_INT128, which puts the 128-bit product together from 32-bit halves; the builds of the model compile the arm with unsigned \_\_int128 (Ratpoints.Sieve.exactScale)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{4523}{4528}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPointsVerbose}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPointsVerbose}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and the start of \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn, and the rest of which is \texttt{Ratpoints.findPointsWork}. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), returned apart from the outcome with the data of the callback, for the negative codes of the library (\texttt{RATPOINTS\_NON\_SQUAREFREE} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_BAD\_ARGS}; \texttt{RATPOINTS\_WORK\_LENGTH\_TOO\_SMALL} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_MEMORY} cannot arise), which share the \texttt{long} that \texttt{find\_points} returns with the count, the caller keeping its data behind the pointer \texttt{info}: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height} of the arguments (\texttt{ratpoints.h:362}), so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses; a height that is not a \texttt{long}, \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63} or more, is refused with error 4, as the program refuses it when it reads the height (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}), where the library cannot be given one, its height being a \texttt{long}. The end of the type \texttt{ratpoints\_args} (\texttt{ratpoints.h:399-{}400}) with its first fields, whose other fields are those of the options, the parameters, the result of the choice of the moduli and the outcome (\texttt{Ratpoints.Options}, \texttt{Ratpoints.SieveOptions}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Params}, \texttt{Ratpoints.SievingInfo}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), of the divisor set-up (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.setupUs1}), or excluded. A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller but the data of the callback, the count, three bits of the flags, the search intervals and the numbers of the moduli used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), which are \texttt{0} unless the search sets them, as \texttt{find\_points\_work} zeroes them on entry with the working field \texttt{sp3}, so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the callback a function that returns what the call gives (\texttt{Ratpoints.Answer}), and its data a value, for the pointer \texttt{info}; the bit \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} of the flags as the print channel \texttt{print}, a function that prints a text into the data of the callback, which holds the standard output of the caller, so that the text comes between the points as on the standard output of the C program, and which prints nothing when the bit is clear; the options of the output as fields of the options (\texttt{Ratpoints.Options}), copied into the flags of the check (\texttt{Ratpoints.CheckFlags}) with the flag of the reversal, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags} that the mask of line 4606 keeps; the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.sturmRegion}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{5219}{5220}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPointsVerbose}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPointsVerbose}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and the start of \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn, and the rest of which is \texttt{Ratpoints.findPointsWork}. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), returned apart from the outcome with the data of the callback, for the negative codes of the library (\texttt{RATPOINTS\_NON\_SQUAREFREE} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_BAD\_ARGS}; \texttt{RATPOINTS\_WORK\_LENGTH\_TOO\_SMALL} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_MEMORY} cannot arise), which share the \texttt{long} that \texttt{find\_points} returns with the count, the caller keeping its data behind the pointer \texttt{info}: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height} of the arguments (\texttt{ratpoints.h:362}), so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses; a height that is not a \texttt{long}, \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63} or more, is refused with error 4, as the program refuses it when it reads the height (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}), where the library cannot be given one, its height being a \texttt{long}. The end of the type \texttt{ratpoints\_args} (\texttt{ratpoints.h:399-{}400}) with its first fields, whose other fields are those of the options, the parameters, the result of the choice of the moduli and the outcome (\texttt{Ratpoints.Options}, \texttt{Ratpoints.SieveOptions}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Params}, \texttt{Ratpoints.SievingInfo}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), of the divisor set-up (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.setupUs1}), or excluded. A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller but the data of the callback, the count, three bits of the flags, the search intervals and the numbers of the moduli used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), which are \texttt{0} unless the search sets them, as \texttt{find\_points\_work} zeroes them on entry with the working field \texttt{sp3}, so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the callback a function that returns what the call gives (\texttt{Ratpoints.Answer}), and its data a value, for the pointer \texttt{info}; the bit \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} of the flags as the print channel \texttt{print}, a function that prints a text into the data of the callback, which holds the standard output of the caller, so that the text comes between the points as on the standard output of the C program, and which prints nothing when the bit is clear; the options of the output as fields of the options (\texttt{Ratpoints.Options}), copied into the flags of the check (\texttt{Ratpoints.CheckFlags}) with the flag of the reversal, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags} that the mask of line 4606 keeps; the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.sturmRegion}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet.)

\section*{\texttt{sturm.c}}
\begin{itemize}
\item \csource{sturm.c}{29}{32}: excluded (other): the includes of math.h, stdlib.h and the header of the library; the model has no headers
\item \csource{sturm.c}{67}{84}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sturm.evalSign}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sturm.evalSign}: the row as an array of integers, for the GMP integers \texttt{cofs} and the \texttt{long} \texttt{degree}, which is the size of the array less one; integers for the GMP integers \texttt{work[0]} and \texttt{work[1]}, the multiplication by a power of 2 for \texttt{mpz\_mul\_2exp}, and \texttt{Int.sign} for \texttt{mpz\_sgn}; \texttt{Int64} for the \texttt{long}s \texttt{num}, \texttt{denexp} and \texttt{e}; the steps counted up from \texttt{0} to \texttt{deg -{} 1}, for the index \texttt{n} that counts down; no scratch integers of the arguments.)
\item \csource{sturm.c}{86}{97}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sturm.computeSturm}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sturm.computeSturm}: the coefficients, the degree, the depth and the search intervals as arguments, for the fields \texttt{cof}, \texttt{degree}, \texttt{sturm}, \texttt{domain} and \texttt{num\_inter} of the arguments; natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s \texttt{degree} and \texttt{iter}, which is from \texttt{0} to \texttt{55} (the search clamps it, \texttt{find\_points.c:4682}); the result as an option of an array, for the \texttt{long} that the C code returns and the intervals it writes into \texttt{domain} with their number \texttt{num\_inter}: none for \texttt{-{}1}, the empty array for \texttt{0}, with \texttt{num\_inter = 0}, and else the intervals, their number the return value; the table of the chain made by \texttt{Ratpoints.Sturm.chain}, whose rows the step reads, for the table on the stack with the degrees, which \texttt{\_ratpoints\_compute\_sturm} fills itself, the index of the last row the size of the chain less one, for the \texttt{k} of line 163; the array of the intervals kept made by \texttt{Ratpoints.Sturm.iterate}, for the array \texttt{ivlocal} on the stack of \texttt{1 + ⌊degree / 2⌋} intervals; integers for the GMP integers and \texttt{Int.sign} for \texttt{mpz\_sgn}; no \texttt{mpz\_init} and \texttt{mpz\_clear}, no copy of the caller's intervals on the heap and no failure for lack of memory (\texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_MEMORY}), which the model cannot meet.)
\item \csource{sturm.c}{99}{163}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sturm.chain}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sturm.chain}: the rows as arrays of their coefficients up to their degree, for the table of \texttt{(d + 1)\textasciicircum{}2} GMP integers and the array of degrees, with no \texttt{mpz\_init} and \texttt{mpz\_clear} (a chain has at most \texttt{d + 1} rows, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sturm.IsChain.size\_le}, and its row \texttt{k + 1} at most \texttt{d -{} k} entries, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sturm.IsChain.size\_getElem!\_add\_one\_add\_le}): an array has one entry more than the degree of its row, and a remainder that becomes zero is the empty array, where the degree in the C code reaches \texttt{-{}1}; a reduction step drops the leading coefficient, which it makes \texttt{0}, where the C code lowers the degree; the rows are handed back, and \texttt{none} for the return of \texttt{-{}1}, where \texttt{\_ratpoints\_compute\_sturm} keeps them in its table for the rest of the Sturm step (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sturm.computeSturm}), and the index of the last row, which the C code leaves in \texttt{k} and sets to \texttt{d} after the loop for \texttt{d = 1}, is the size of the array less one; a list of integers for the array of GMP integers of the coefficients, local values for the scratch integers \texttt{work[0]}, \texttt{work[1]} and \texttt{work[2]}, and Lean's \texttt{/} for \texttt{mpz\_fdiv\_q}, which agree on the divisions of the chain, all exact.)

\section*{\texttt{rp-private.h}}
\begin{itemize}
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{30}{35}: excluded (other): the includes of the headers of the C library, among them float.h and math.h of the doubles of the search intervals; the model has no headers
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{41}{43}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.fitsLong}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.fitsLong}: the bounds of a \texttt{long} of 64 bits, fixed, where the C code does not compile unless an \texttt{unsigned long} has exactly 64 bits.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{47}{47}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.fitsLong}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.fitsLong}: the bounds of a \texttt{long} of 64 bits, fixed, where the C code does not compile unless an \texttt{unsigned long} has exactly 64 bits.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{49}{51}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.rbaLength}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.rbaLength}: computed from \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaPack}, where each build sets \texttt{RBA\_LENGTH} by a literal, and the build with 64-bit bit arrays by \texttt{LONG\_LENGTH}, and its logarithm \texttt{RBA\_SHIFT} likewise (\texttt{Ratpoints.rbaShift}); the shifts by \texttt{RBA\_SHIFT} and by \texttt{LONG\_SHIFT} are divisions by \texttt{rbaLength} and by 64, which round down also for a negative value, as the arithmetic shifts of gcc do, and the masks by \texttt{RBA\_LENGTH -{} 1} and by \texttt{LONG\_MASK} Euclidean remainders.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{55}{58}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.rbaPack}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.rbaPack}: the value of the default build, set here, where the C code chooses the build by the macros that the compiler is given; the vector type of a bit array becomes \texttt{rbaPack} consecutive words of an array of \texttt{UInt64}.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{60}{60}: excluded (other): the include of the header of the library; the model has no headers
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{76}{84}: excluded (threads): the atomic loads and stores of the fields that the threads of a pool share (RP\_ACQUIRE, RP\_RELAXED, RP\_PUBLISH), and their plain forms for a build without threads; on one thread an atomic load or store is a plain read or write, which the model makes
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{86}{86}: excluded (other): FLOOR, which the C code uses nowhere: find\_points.c names it only in a comment
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{87}{87}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Setup.slope}, \lname{Ratpoints.arraySizeAt}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Setup.slope}: integers for the \texttt{int}s, and the slope as a natural number; no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.arraySizeAt}: a \texttt{Nat} for the \texttt{long} field, so that only \texttt{0} stands for the default, which the library takes for every value \texttt{≤ 0}; \texttt{64} for \texttt{LONG\_LENGTH}; and the macro \texttt{CEIL} of a natural number \texttt{x} by \texttt{d} as \texttt{(x + d -{} 1) / d}, which is its value for every \texttt{x ≥ 0}.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{113}{113}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.rbaPack}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.rbaPack}: the value of the default build, set here, where the C code chooses the build by the macros that the compiler is given; the vector type of a bit array becomes \texttt{rbaPack} consecutive words of an array of \texttt{UInt64}.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{123}{123}: excluded (other): the include of the vector intrinsics in the build USE\_AVX512, with 512-bit bit arrays; the word operations of the model need none
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{125}{125}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.rbaLength}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.rbaLength}: computed from \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaPack}, where each build sets \texttt{RBA\_LENGTH} by a literal, and the build with 64-bit bit arrays by \texttt{LONG\_LENGTH}, and its logarithm \texttt{RBA\_SHIFT} likewise (\texttt{Ratpoints.rbaShift}); the shifts by \texttt{RBA\_SHIFT} and by \texttt{LONG\_SHIFT} are divisions by \texttt{rbaLength} and by 64, which round down also for a negative value, as the arithmetic shifts of gcc do, and the masks by \texttt{RBA\_LENGTH -{} 1} and by \texttt{LONG\_MASK} Euclidean remainders.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{126}{126}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.rbaShift}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.rbaShift}: the value of the default build, set here, where each build sets it by a literal, and the build with 64-bit bit arrays by \texttt{LONG\_SHIFT}; the model shifts by none of them: the shifts by \texttt{RBA\_SHIFT} are divisions by \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaLength}.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{127}{128}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.rbaPack}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.rbaPack}: the value of the default build, set here, where the C code chooses the build by the macros that the compiler is given; the vector type of a bit array becomes \texttt{rbaPack} consecutive words of an array of \texttt{UInt64}.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{129}{132}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andRows}, \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andRowsChunked}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andRows}: the bit arrays set to the class word by a loop that counts up, bit array \texttt{n -{} 1 -{} i} at the step \texttt{i}, for the loop that counts down from the last; the class word written into each word of a bit array, for the vector \texttt{RBA(packed)} that \texttt{get\_2adic\_info} makes once per class (\texttt{find\_points.c:1098}) and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} copies into each bit array (\texttt{bits64}, \texttt{sift.c:519}, \texttt{sift.c:954}); the moduli of the stage with their rows and their reciprocals as two lists, for the first \texttt{sp1} sieve specs and the array \texttt{magics} from position \texttt{0} on; the value \texttt{-{}w\_low -{} offset} written out in both reductions, for the \texttt{long} \texttt{a}, which stays a \texttt{long} where the helper \texttt{mod} reduces it outside \texttt{small} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.fitsLong\_neg\_sub}); indices for the pointers into the rows and into the survivors, and the number of whole periods and the rest computed before their loops; natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; a Boolean for the \texttt{int} \texttt{small}; no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andRowsChunked}: no moduli tested by the size of the local array of the sieve specs, for \texttt{sp1 == 0}; the bit arrays set to the class word by a loop that counts up, bit array \texttt{n -{} 1 -{} i} at the step \texttt{i}, for the loop that counts down from the last; the class word written into each word of a bit array, for the vector \texttt{RBA(packed)} that \texttt{get\_2adic\_info} makes once per class (\texttt{find\_points.c:1098}) and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} copies into each bit array (\texttt{bits64}, \texttt{sift.c:519}); the end of the whole chunks the index \texttt{full}, for the word number \texttt{w\_high\_full}, which is also the index of the first bit array of the tail, for the pointer \texttt{surv} after the chunks; natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{133}{133}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}: indices for the pointers into the survivors, and a scan that holds its position as an index, where ratpoints recovers the word number from a pointer difference; the copy \texttt{nums} of the bit array a vector of \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaPack} words; the sentinel \texttt{\textasciitilde{}zero} of every build as \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaPack} words \texttt{\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}0}, written one at a time; natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; the counters \texttt{cnt} passed and returned, for the field \texttt{n\_arrays} of the sieving thread, which counts one up for each bit array that is not zero (line 1092); the delivery \texttt{r} passed and returned, for the pointers \texttt{info} and \texttt{wk-{}>quit} and the count \texttt{total} of \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0}, and the flag \texttt{quit} tested after each bit array, where the C code returns from \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} within the walk through the set bits of a word (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.walkWord}).)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{134}{134}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andBitArray}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andBitArray}: one definition for every build, on bit arrays given by their indices in arrays of words, each bit array \texttt{rbaPack} consecutive words, for the \texttt{\&} on the vector type of the build.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{135}{136}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.siftBitArrayWhole}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.siftBitArrayWhole}: the stride, the first numerator and the steps as natural numbers and integers, the powers \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} k} for the shifts \texttt{1L << k}, \texttt{RBA\_LENGTH << k} and \texttt{LONG\_LENGTH << k}, the last two of which stay \texttt{int}s, while the first numerators of the words, the numerators of bits of the bit arrays of a height bound below \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63}, stay \texttt{long}s (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.NumClass.fitsLong\_numerator}); the words of the bit array read as entries of the vector, for \texttt{EXT0} and \texttt{EXT}; natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; the delivery \texttt{r} passed and returned, for the pointers \texttt{info} and \texttt{wk-{}>quit} and the count \texttt{total} of \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0}, and the flag \texttt{quit} tested after each walk through the set bits of a word and the rest of the bit array left at a stop, where the C code returns from \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} within the walk (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.walkWord}); no counts under \texttt{RP\_PHASE\_COUNTS} and no stop after a phase (\texttt{RP\_STOP\_AFTER}).)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{137}{152}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.isZeroAt}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.isZeroAt}: one definition for every build, on a bit array given by its index in an array of words, \texttt{rbaPack} consecutive words that it compares with \texttt{0} one at a time, for the tests of the builds on the vector type, with vector instructions or by or-ing its words; the test for zero \texttt{TESTZ} also stands for its negation \texttt{TEST}.)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andRows}: the bit arrays set to the class word by a loop that counts up, bit array \texttt{n -{} 1 -{} i} at the step \texttt{i}, for the loop that counts down from the last; the class word written into each word of a bit array, for the vector \texttt{RBA(packed)} that \texttt{get\_2adic\_info} makes once per class (\texttt{find\_points.c:1098}) and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} copies into each bit array (\texttt{bits64}, \texttt{sift.c:519}, \texttt{sift.c:954}); the moduli of the stage with their rows and their reciprocals as two lists, for the first \texttt{sp1} sieve specs and the array \texttt{magics} from position \texttt{0} on; the value \texttt{-{}w\_low -{} offset} written out in both reductions, for the \texttt{long} \texttt{a}, which stays a \texttt{long} where the helper \texttt{mod} reduces it outside \texttt{small} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.fitsLong\_neg\_sub}); indices for the pointers into the rows and into the survivors, and the number of whole periods and the rest computed before their loops; natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; a Boolean for the \texttt{int} \texttt{small}; no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andRowsChunked}: no moduli tested by the size of the local array of the sieve specs, for \texttt{sp1 == 0}; the bit arrays set to the class word by a loop that counts up, bit array \texttt{n -{} 1 -{} i} at the step \texttt{i}, for the loop that counts down from the last; the class word written into each word of a bit array, for the vector \texttt{RBA(packed)} that \texttt{get\_2adic\_info} makes once per class (\texttt{find\_points.c:1098}) and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} copies into each bit array (\texttt{bits64}, \texttt{sift.c:519}); the end of the whole chunks the index \texttt{full}, for the word number \texttt{w\_high\_full}, which is also the index of the first bit array of the tail, for the pointer \texttt{surv} after the chunks; natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{205}{205}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}: indices for the pointers into the survivors, and a scan that holds its position as an index, where ratpoints recovers the word number from a pointer difference; the copy \texttt{nums} of the bit array a vector of \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaPack} words; the sentinel \texttt{\textasciitilde{}zero} of every build as \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaPack} words \texttt{\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}0}, written one at a time; natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; the counters \texttt{cnt} passed and returned, for the field \texttt{n\_arrays} of the sieving thread, which counts one up for each bit array that is not zero (line 1092); the delivery \texttt{r} passed and returned, for the pointers \texttt{info} and \texttt{wk-{}>quit} and the count \texttt{total} of \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0}, and the flag \texttt{quit} tested after each bit array, where the C code returns from \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} within the walk through the set bits of a word (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.walkWord}).)

\item \csource{rp-private.h}{542}{555}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry}, \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry}: only the fields that the rows of a prime read; the rows of the residues, which ratpoints keeps in the field \texttt{sieve}, that of \texttt{0} from the build and the others made by \texttt{init} when a denominator first needs them, are kept in the table of rows of the prime in the store of the run (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.EntryRef.prime}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.primeRows}), from which the run reads them and into which it builds them (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.setRows}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.buildRows}); the fields \texttt{init}, \texttt{magic}, \texttt{nf}, \texttt{factor} and \texttt{pw} are those of the sieve entry \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry}, of which the prime is the single factor, and so are \texttt{bias}, \texttt{rbainv}, \texttt{dinv} and the density \texttt{r}.)
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry}: the kinds of modulus as the list of the factors: one prime factor for a prime, whose entry has \texttt{nf = 0} and the tables \texttt{is\_f\_square} and \texttt{inverses} of its own; one prime-power factor for a prime power, whose entry has \texttt{nf = 1} and its tables \texttt{pw}; and two or more for a product, whose entry has \texttt{nf ≥ 2} and points to the entries \texttt{factor} of its factors; no bound \texttt{RP\_MAX\_FACTORS} on the number of factors, which the choice of the moduli keeps when it offers a composite modulus (\texttt{Ratpoints.takeFactor}); the rows of the residues, which ratpoints keeps in the array \texttt{sieve} of the entry, kept in the store of the run (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.RowStore}) in the table of rows of the reference \texttt{ref}; the reference \texttt{ref} to the entry whose table of rows holds its rows (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.EntryRef}), for the pointer to the entry: a prime or a prime power that of its one factor, so that the modulus and the products with it as a factor read one table of rows, as they read one entry in the C code, and a product its own; the kind of its builder \texttt{init} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.RowInit}), for the pointer to the function; a natural number for the \texttt{unsigned long} reciprocal \texttt{magic}, and natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s \texttt{bias} and \texttt{rbainv}; the inverses \texttt{dinv} an array, for the array of \texttt{RP\_NUM\_STRIDES} \texttt{long}s, which the row offsets of the packing fill (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.classOffsets}) with an entry for each stride up to the largest in use, where the entries of the C code beyond it stay unset and unread; the density \texttt{r}, which the correction of the moduli during the run reads (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.adaptPrimes}), a \texttt{Float} for the \texttt{double}, and the count \texttt{nf} of the factors, an integer for the \texttt{long}, \texttt{0} for a prime, \texttt{1} for a prime power and the number of factors for a product, kept with the list of the factors.)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Outcome}: a structure for what the C code returns and writes back into the arguments: the data of the callback, which the caller has behind its pointer \texttt{info}, the count, which \texttt{find\_points} returns as a \texttt{long} that also carries its error codes (\texttt{Ratpoints.findPointsWith} returns the refusals apart), Booleans for three bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags}, and the search intervals as a list, for the array \texttt{args-{}>domain} and the number \texttt{args-{}>num\_inter} that the search writes back and the program reads after it; nor the private fields that \texttt{sieving\_info} and \texttt{adapt\_primes} write, \texttt{adapt\_at}, \texttt{run\_words}, \texttt{run\_denoms}, \texttt{sp3\_max} and \texttt{check\_rel}, which nothing reads before \texttt{sieving\_info} sets them again in the next search; \item \csource{ratpoints.h}{399}{400}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPointsVerbose}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPointsVerbose}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and the start of \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn, and the rest of which is \texttt{Ratpoints.findPointsWork}. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), returned apart from the outcome with the data of the callback, for the negative codes of the library (\texttt{RATPOINTS\_NON\_SQUAREFREE} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_BAD\_ARGS}; \texttt{RATPOINTS\_WORK\_LENGTH\_TOO\_SMALL} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_MEMORY} cannot arise), which share the \texttt{long} that \texttt{find\_points} returns with the count, the caller keeping its data behind the pointer \texttt{info}: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height} of the arguments (\texttt{ratpoints.h:362}), so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses; a height that is not a \texttt{long}, \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63} or more, is refused with error 4, as the program refuses it when it reads the height (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}), where the library cannot be given one, its height being a \texttt{long}. The end of the type \texttt{ratpoints\_args} (\texttt{ratpoints.h:399-{}400}) with its first fields, whose other fields are those of the options, the parameters, the result of the choice of the moduli and the outcome (\texttt{Ratpoints.Options}, \texttt{Ratpoints.SieveOptions}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Params}, \texttt{Ratpoints.SievingInfo}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), of the divisor set-up (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.setupUs1}), or excluded. A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller but the data of the callback, the count, three bits of the flags, the search intervals and the numbers of the moduli used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), which are \texttt{0} unless the search sets them, as \texttt{find\_points\_work} zeroes them on entry with the working field \texttt{sp3}, so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the callback a function that returns what the call gives (\texttt{Ratpoints.Answer}), and its data a value, for the pointer \texttt{info}; the bit \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} of the flags as the print channel \texttt{print}, a function that prints a text into the data of the callback, which holds the standard output of the caller, so that the text comes between the points as on the standard output of the C program, and which prints nothing when the bit is clear; the options of the output as fields of the options (\texttt{Ratpoints.Options}), copied into the flags of the check (\texttt{Ratpoints.CheckFlags}) with the flag of the reversal, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags} that the mask of line 4606 keeps; the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.sturmRegion}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet.)
